notes:
Sync goes live: edits now appear on your other open devices in about two seconds.

**New**

- **Realtime sync (dev).** Your devices now hold a lightweight, end-to-end-private connection to the sync server. Edit a note on your desktop and the same note updates on your open laptop or phone in **~2 seconds** — no more waiting for the next sync interval. Your edits also upload within a few seconds of you pausing (instead of only when you switch away), and the sync status quietly shows "Synced · live" while the connection is up. If the connection drops — sleep, bad Wi-Fi, a server restart — the app silently falls back to the previous scheduled syncing and reconnects on its own; nothing is ever lost either way, because the connection only *hurries* sync along, it never replaces the careful bookkeeping underneath. (PRD Addendum 31 §AB, phase R1.)

**Under the hood**

- The realtime channel is a notify-only WebSocket: the server fans out a content-free "your vault has news" nudge (a sequence number, nothing else) after each push, and receiving devices run the normal pull cycle — ops never travel over the socket and cursors remain the source of truth, so a lost nudge costs seconds, never correctness. Client behavior: jittered exponential reconnect (1s→60s cap), bounded connect deadlines with fresh-socket retries, 500ms nudge coalescing, push-after-edit debounce (3s quiet / 15s max) active only while connected, and the periodic cadence relaxing to its 15-minute floor while live. Load-checked at 2,000 concurrent sockets (fan-out to all in under 20ms; ~8MB resident). Behind the `realtime` gradual-rollout flag (dev-on; flag-off is byte-identical to 0.6.22, pinned by tests) riding the dev-only `sync` gate. Server deployed with the matching `/v1/realtime` endpoint. Convergence proven in the sync simulator (94/94 incl. nudge-driven, dropped-nudge, and reconnect-storm scenarios). (#654.)
